name: Don Julio Blanco
place: Atotonilco el Alto, in the Jalisco Highlands, Mexico

facts.base: Blue agave from the Jalisco Highlands, roasted in brick ovens and fermented with Don Julio's own yeast
facts.age: Unaged: bottled after distillation, cut only with water
facts.law: Tequila, 100% blue agave, under Mexico's denomination of origin; blanco means unaged or rested under two months

made: Don Julio is made from blue agave grown in the highlands around Atotonilco el Alto. The piñas are roasted slowly in brick ovens, for about three days by most accounts, then crushed, and the juice is fermented with a yeast strain of Don Julio's own. The wash is distilled twice in pot stills, and the Blanco is cut with water and bottled unaged: three ingredients, agave, water and yeast, and the base every other Don Julio is built on.
taste: Crisp cooked agave and citrus on the nose, lemon and grapefruit peel with a little green pepper. The palate is clean and lightly sweet, agave, lime and white pepper, with a fresh, peppery finish.

lines.s10: Don Julio Blanco is an unaged 100% blue agave tequila from the Jalisco Highlands: crisp agave, citrus and pepper.
lines.s20: Don Julio Blanco is unaged tequila made from highland blue agave, roasted in brick ovens, fermented with Don Julio's own yeast and distilled twice. Crisp and clean, it tastes of cooked agave, citrus peel and pepper, and it makes a bright Margarita.
lines.s45: This is Don Julio Blanco, named for Don Julio González, who began making tequila in 1942 in Atotonilco el Alto, in the highlands of Jalisco. The blue agave is roasted slowly in brick ovens, fermented with Don Julio's own yeast and distilled twice, then bottled unaged, the base of every Don Julio. In the glass it is crisp cooked agave, lemon and grapefruit peel and white pepper, clean and lightly sweet. We pour it neat at room temperature, over one large cube, or in a Margarita or a Paloma. The short, round bottle was made low, the story goes, so guests could see each other across the table.
lines.sale: Don Julio Blanco is crisp highland agave with lemon peel and white pepper, the base of every Don Julio. Taste it neat, or let it lead a Margarita with fresh lime.

serve.neat: Neat at room temperature, about an ounce and a half, sipped rather than shot.
serve.rocks: Over one large cube, or long with soda and a squeeze of lime.
serve.glass: A copita or a small tulip neat; a rocks glass over ice.
serve.classic: The Margarita, the Paloma and the Spicy Margarita; also Ranch Water.

guest: Don Julio Blanco is an unaged tequila of 100% blue agave from the Jalisco Highlands: crisp cooked agave, citrus peel and pepper, clean enough to sip neat.
story: Don Julio González began making tequila in 1942, at seventeen, in Atotonilco el Alto, and his first distillery was called La Primavera, the springtime. In 1987 his family launched a tequila under his own name, the first Don Julio. The squat bottle, the story goes, was made short so that it would not block the view across a family table. The Blanco is the base of the whole range: every aged Don Julio begins as this spirit.
watch: Blanco, silver and plata are one category: unaged, or rested under two months. The 1942 on this label is the founder's start, not an age.
Not Don Julio 1942: a guest who asks for the 1942 means the tall añejo, not this squat bottle with the blue band.
The Blanco and the Reposado share the squat bottle: read the band, blue for the Blanco and copper for the Reposado, before pouring.

recall.prompt: What is Don Julio Blanco, and how is it made?
recall.answer: An unaged 100% blue agave tequila from Atotonilco el Alto in the Jalisco Highlands: agave roasted in brick ovens, fermented with Don Julio's own yeast, distilled twice and bottled at 40% ABV. Crisp agave, citrus and pepper; neat, on one cube, or in a Margarita.

quiz.q: In which Jalisco town is Don Julio made?
quiz.explain: Atotonilco el Alto, in the highlands of Jalisco, where Don Julio González began making tequila in 1942.

quiz.q: Why, as the story goes, was the Don Julio bottle made short?
options: So guests could see across the table
To fit beneath a low back bar
To save glass in a wartime shortage
To travel safely by mule train
quiz.explain: So it would not block the view across a family table: a low bottle keeps the conversation open.

quiz.q: How long does Don Julio Blanco rest in oak?
options: It is not aged in wood
quiz.explain: It is bottled unaged. Eight months is the Reposado's time in American oak.
